channel.title: Up First from NPR
channel.description:
NPR's Up First is the news you need to start your day. The three biggest stories of the day, with reporting and analysis from NPR News — in 10 minutes. Available weekdays at 6:30 a.m. ET, with hosts Leila Fadel, Steve Inskeep, Michel Martin and A Martinez. Also available on Saturdays at 9 a.m. ET, with Ayesha Rascoe and Scott Simon. On Sundays, hear a longer exploration behind the headlines with Ayesha Rascoe on "The Sunday Story," available by 8 a.m. ET. Subscribe and listen, then support your local NPR station at donate.npr.org.

Support public media by joining NPR+ at plus.npr.org. You’ll get perks for over 25 NPR podcasts, including sponsor-free listening for Up First, NPR News Now, and more.

item.title: Nvidia's Future, Trump's Ties to Huang, US Mediates Russia-Ukraine Talks
item.description:
Nvidia founder Jensen Huang is out as CEO after allegations involving multiple affairs, leaving longtime CFO Colette Kress to steady the company as it faces questions about leadership, investor confidence and its dominance of the AI chip market.
Huang’s close relationship with President Trump is drawing scrutiny in Washington, with lawmakers asking whether his access influenced U.S. chip policy toward China and what administration officials knew about the national security concerns surrounding him.
U.S. envoys say European governments could join the next round of Russia-Ukraine talks after meetings with Vladimir Putin and Volodymyr Zelenskyy, as negotiators test whether a broader European security framework can help break the deadlock over the war.

Want more analysis of the most important news of the day, plus a little fun? Subscribe to the Up First newsletter.

item.title: Abdul El-Sayed: Democrats need to ‘earn’ their mandate | Newsmakers
item.description:
Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed says Americans “temporarily” put their trust and hope in Democrats.

But he adds that if his party doesn’t act boldly when it takes control of Congress, it may lose that trust.

El-Sayed is the first Muslim to be elected to the U.S. Senate. The 42-year-old progressive from Michigan is now calling for new Senate leadership and urging President Trump to meet and discuss how they can “figure out what we can work on and get done.”

El-Sayed, a former Detroit public health official, even floated the idea of naming major healthcare legislation after Trump. 

“Put his name on it,” El-Sayed said. “He'll probably pass it. I'm not above doing that. I don't care what it's called.”

In this episode from NPR’s Newsmakers, El-Sayed sat down with NPR host Leila Fadel to talk about a divisive campaign season, the future of the Democratic Party and how Congress should legislate during the final two years of Trump’s term in the White House. Find more episodes of Newsmakers on Spotify, Apple, YouTube, or wherever you get podcasts.

item.title: Colom Wins Mississippi, Trump Warns Incoming Democrats, Russia-Ukraine Talks
item.description:
Democrat Scott Colom won Mississippi’s Senate race by fewer than 5,000 votes, becoming the state’s first Black senator since Reconstruction and ending a more than 40-year stretch without a Democrat in the seat.
The White House is warning Democrats that their planned investigations could cross into “blatant criminality,” previewing a legal and political fight over congressional oversight when Democrats take control next year.
Russia and Ukraine agreed to a major prisoner exchange after two days of U.S.-mediated talks, as American envoys meet Vladimir Putin and Volodymyr Zelenskyy to explore whether a broader European security agreement could help end the war.

item.title: Hegseth Impeachment Blocked, House Leadership Change, DOJ Charges Terror Suspects
item.description:
House Republicans blocked an effort to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, but lawmakers still have other ways to challenge the administration over the Iran war and its push for more defense spending.
House Republicans chose Ohio Congressman Jim Jordan to lead them in the minority, signaling a more combative approach as the party prepares to face a Democratic majority next year.
Federal prosecutors say three Iran-backed operatives were involved in nearly twenty attacks or attempted attacks across Europe and the United States, while a separate case involving a U.S. soldier accused of spying for Russia is raising new security concerns in Britain.

item.title: Hegseth Impeachment Push, Trump Holds Off Iran Strikes, Congress Summons Nvidia's CEO
item.description:
The House could vote this week on impeaching Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over allegations that he violated federal law and Congress’ war powers, even as President Trump continues to stand by him.
Trump says U.S. allies in the Middle East want him to hold off on more strikes against Iran while talks continue, even as he warns the U.S. remains “locked and loaded” if that changes.
Congress is demanding answers from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang as scrutiny grows over his relationship with a woman tied to a company reportedly investigated over whether restricted Nvidia chips were reaching China.

Want more analysis of the most important news of the day, plus a little fun? Subscribe to the Up First newsletter.

item.title: Trump's Post-Midterm Changes, Lame-Duck Congress, Nvidia Huang Investigation
item.description:
President Trump says his immigration crackdown may have gone too far even as he elevates Stephen Miller, one of its chief architects, to run the White House after Republicans lost Congress.
Republicans are returning to Washington for a lame-duck session with a shrinking House majority and a short list of priorities, including funding the government, passing military spending and confirming Trump nominees.
Nvidia is investigating reports that CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with a woman suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence, raising new questions about one of the most important companies in the U.S.-China technology race.

Want more analysis of the most important news of the day, plus a little fun? Subscribe to the Up First newsletter.
